draft.title: Tables and graphs
card: A results table has a title and a heading for each column, with units. The independent variable (the one you change) goes in the first column. The dependent variable (the one you measure) goes next.
suits continuous data, which are numbers that can take any value on a scale, such as time or temperature. Points are joined to show how the measurement changes.
suits categories, which are separate groups, such as types of soil or colours. Each category gets its own column, and the columns do not join.
On a graph, the independent variable goes on the horizontal axis and the dependent variable goes on the vertical axis. Each axis has a label and units.
draft.remember: Independent variable first in the table. Line graph for continuous data, column graph for categories.

a.q: Priya times how long ice takes to melt in four liquids: water, salt water, juice and milk. Which graph suits her results?
opts: A column graph, because the liquids are categories
A line graph, because the liquids are categories
A column graph, because the times are continuous
A line graph, because the times are measured in seconds
a.why: The liquids are separate groups, so each one gets its own column. A line graph is the tempting choice because the melting times are numbers, but the numbers are the dependent variable. The liquids on the horizontal axis decide the graph type.
a.clue: Look at what she changes: are the liquids a scale or separate groups?

b.q: Tom heats water and records its temperature every minute for ten minutes. How should he set out his table and graph?
opts: Time in the first column, and a line graph
Temperature in the first column, and a line graph
Time in the first column, and a column graph
Temperature in the first column, and a column graph
b.why: Tom chooses the times, so time is the independent variable and goes first. Time is continuous, so a line graph shows how temperature changes. Putting temperature first is tempting because it is the main result, but it is the variable he measures.
b.clue: Which variable did Tom choose, and is it a scale or a group?

a.best: A column graph, because the liquids are categories

b.best: Time in the first column, and a line graph
